column2: M120 site declaration — every data-raw harness that RESUMES from a checkpoint.
A site here reads a cache back and may therefore serve rows the current design
never computed; harnesses that only WRITE a checkpoint are deliberately absent
(they cannot serve a stale row). This file is the declared enumeration AC4
quantifies over — it is not, and never claims to be, a discovery procedure over
all harnesses. That job belongs to the run-time trace in checkpoint-guard.R,
which observes deserializations rather than spellings.
The deserialization list AC2 quantifies over. A declared site, and every
non-package file it source()s other than the guard, may call none of these:
each returns an R object from bytes on disk, so each is a way to serve a
cached row the current design never computed. The list is an ENUMERATION and
says nothing about a name outside it; the checker refuses to run unless it
contains at least the four required names, so it cannot be quietly shortened
to whatever the sites happen not to use.
readRDS,load,unserialize,readr::read_rds
A guard call counts only where something REACHES it. Reachability starts at
live top-level code and follows calls; a function handed BY NAME to one of
these appliers is reached too, since m111's ckpt_read() is reached only
through `mclapply(cells, run_cell)` and a direct-calls-only rule would go
vacuous on exactly that site. The list WEAKENS nothing on its own — it can
only make more code reachable — but it is declared rather than assumed so a
handoff form outside it is a visible gap rather than a silent pass.
lapply,sapply,vapply,mapply,Map,mclapply,parLapply,do.call,Reduce,Filter
Liveness. A branch counts only when its condition is literally TRUE or is one
of these declared idioms, each with its reason; `if (0)`, `if (FALSE ||
FALSE)` and `if (getOption("x", FALSE))` are none of the three and park a
call rather than make it. This list WEAKENS the check, so each entry states
why the branch is a real execution path and not a disabling switch:
sys.nframe() == 0L — the run-as-a-script entry-point block every harness
here uses; by parse it is indistinguishable from a disabling condition,
which is why it must be declared rather than inferred.
file.exists(ckpt) — the resume path itself: a harness reads its cache only
when the cache is there, so this is the branch the guard exists to check.
sys.nframe() == 0L,file.exists(ckpt)
The mutation forms the self-test plants, on every declared site and once per
name in that site's api column. The checker refuses to self-test unless the
list contains the forms AC4 requires, so the probe cannot shrink to the forms
that happen to pass. Each form removes the site's live guard call and then
tries to make the checker believe the call is still there:
deleted                — removed outright, nothing put back
dead-copy              — a copy kept in an `if (FALSE)` branch
parked-unreached       — a copy in a function nothing calls
parked-false-cond      — a copy under `if (0)`, `if (FALSE || FALSE)` and
`if (getOption(...))`, none of them literally false
parked-idiom-unreached — a copy under a DECLARED idiom, inside a function
nothing calls: the idiom must not rescue a call
nothing reaches, or the idiom list would be a
back door into the liveness rule
assert-after-write     — the pre-write assertion moved to just after the
site's first output write, inside the same block
register-non-path      — the registration handed a literal NULL
source-commented       — the source() of the guard commented out
deserialization-planted — one live call of each declared deserialization name
declaration-withdrawn  — a determinant withdrawn from the DECLARATION, the
script left untouched

script       path relative to the repo root
params       the design parameters compared on resume, in the declared order;
the mismatch message names the EARLIEST differing one in this order
roots        the site's ENTRY POINTS into its own generating code. The hashed
block is the call closure of these — every function they reach
that the site itself defines — so a helper added later is covered
without anyone remembering to list it. Package functions stop the
walk: their behavior is pinned by the test suite, not by this hash
values       the non-function determinants, which are declared rather than
derived: seed-offset vectors, sampler argument lists, and the
formula and prior each base fit is compiled from. Following data
references instead would drag in the compiled model object itself
exemptions   determinants the walk reaches but cannot hash, each with its reason
below. Empty on a site with none. This list WEAKENS the check, so
it is the one place a determinant may go uncovered, and it is a
recorded decision rather than a silent omission.
base_fit — a compiled brms/Stan fit; not stably deparsable, and
what determines it (base_formula, base_prior, brm_args) is hashed.
unit         what one checkpoint entry covers
api          the guard calls the site must make — ALL of them, live. A site
that keeps its file-level call and drops its per-entry one has
stopped checking the thing that goes stale, so no single call
stands in for the set
